title: Deploy smoke runs the deployed commit's code with VERCEL_AUTOMATION_BYPASS_SECRET on any successful deployment_status, with no fork or creator guard
description:
The `smoke` job in .github/workflows/deploy-smoke.yml runs on every successful `deployment_status` event. Its only guard is state=='success' plus a non-empty URL. Unlike the secret-bearing jobs in db-checks.yml and deriva.yml, it has no fork exclusion, no deployment-creator or trusted-ref condition, and no `environment:` approval gate.

The job places the repository secret VERCEL_AUTOMATION_BYPASS_SECRET in job-level env. It then checks out the event's default commit, which for deployment_status is the deployed commit, and runs `node scripts/check_deploy.mjs` from that checkout. The AUD-01 host allowlist meant to confine the secret lives inside that same checked-out script, and it reads HOSTS_PROD from the same checked-out app.js. It therefore only constrains an honest commit.

The repository is recorded as public (ADR-0003). Suppose the Vercel GitHub integration builds a pull request from a fork, either automatically or after a team member clicks Authorize under Vercel's Git Fork Protection, and posts its usual GitHub deployment status for the PR head commit. Then:
- The fork author's script would run in this repository's Actions context while holding the bypass secret.
- Even the honest script would send the secret as `x-vercel-protection-bypass` to a preview built from the fork's code.
- If GitHub also takes the workflow definition from the deployment commit, the same trigger would hand every repository secret to fork-authored workflow code, including SUPABASE_BACKUP_DATABASE_URL and the auditor database URLs.

The changelog downgraded AUD-01 because the URL can only come from Vercel or from repository writers. It did not consider who authored the commit being deployed.

Local check-05 rendered the job policy and emulated the final step against a fixture checkout. The rendering showed no guard tokens, no environment, checkout without a ref, and the secret at job level. In the emulation, a check_deploy.mjs that differs from main received the dummy secret through the job env. Whether real fork deployments reach this job is a Vercel and GitHub fact that cannot be observed offline.
claimed_root_cause: A privileged deployment_status job trusts both the code and the deployment of whatever commit the event names. Secret confinement (the host allowlist) is implemented inside the checked-out deployment-commit script and its app.js rather than in trusted workflow configuration. The job has no condition that excludes deployments of commits not authored on this repository's own branches (no fork, creator or trusted-ref guard and no environment gate), while its sibling secret-bearing PR jobs do exclude forks.

trace.description: Any deployment_status event in the repository triggers the workflow. The Vercel app posts these for every deployment it builds, including authorized fork-PR previews.
The guard checks only deployment_status.state == 'success' and a non-empty environment_url or target_url. It has no creator, head-repository/fork or trusted-ref condition.
VERCEL_AUTOMATION_BYPASS_SECRET is pulled from repository secrets into job-level env, visible to every step. No `environment:` gate requires approval.
Checkout has no `ref:` and uses the event default commit, which for deployment_status is the commit being deployed.
Runs `node scripts/check_deploy.mjs` from that checkout while the secret is in the process environment.

The deployed commit's own script reads the secret. Its host allowlist (lines 35-40) comes from the same commit's app.js, so an altered commit is unconstrained. The unaltered script sends the secret as a request header (line 61) to the deployment built from that commit.

evidence.description: The sibling secret-bearing jobs exclude forks with `github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository`. deploy-smoke has no equivalent for deployment events.
HOSTS_PROD for the secret allowlist is read from the LOCAL (checked-out) app.js, the same commit whose deployment is being tested.
Every request to the deployment under test carries `x-vercel-protection-bypass`, so a preview built from untrusted code receives the secret even when the script is honest.
AUD-01 was downgraded because the URL comes from Vercel or from repository writers. The deployed commit's author is not considered.
The decision record says the repository is public, so any GitHub user could open a fork pull request (current visibility is unobserved).
The regression suite only exercises the host allowlist inside a trusted copy of the script. Nothing covers the provenance of the commit the workflow checks out.

blockers: Vercel project setting 'Git Fork Protection' (Project Settings > Security): whether fork-PR previews deploy automatically or only after a team member authorizes them. This is a dashboard fact absent from the repository.

Whether the Vercel GitHub integration creates a GitHub Deployment and a success deployment_status in this repository for an authorized fork-PR preview, and with which sha and ref. This is provider behavior that cannot be observed offline.

Whether GitHub Actions starts deployment_status workflows for such a fork-authored sha with repository secrets. Also whether it reads the workflow definition from the deployment commit, which would extend exposure from the bypass secret to every repository secret, or from the default branch. Both are hosted GitHub facts.

Current repository visibility and fork policy. ADR-0003 records the repository as public, but the run architecture reports GitHub metadata showing it as private. This determines whether any GitHub user or only collaborators can open a fork PR.

Whether Vercel forwards the `x-vercel-protection-bypass` request header to Functions or Middleware of a deployment. This decides the second leg: the secret reaching fork-built deployment code even if the checkout were pinned to trusted code.
Which deployments the configured Protection Bypass for Automation unlocks. This affects the impact of disclosing it.

validation_plan.local: After a fix, re-run a policy rendering like agents/h07-deploy-edge check-05 (PyYAML over deploy-smoke.yml) and assert three things. First, the step that holds VERCEL_AUTOMATION_BYPASS_SECRET runs only code from a trusted ref, for example a second actions/checkout of the default branch for scripts/, with the deployment commit read only as data. Second, the secret is scoped to that single step. Third, the job requires an `environment:` with required reviewers, or a guard that admits only deployments created by vercel[bot] for commits on this repository's own branches. Add a case to tests/deploy-smoke.test.js that fails if the workflow checks out the event commit while exposing the secret.
validation_plan.deployment:
Owner-observed only; do not probe others' infrastructure:
1. In Vercel, read Project Settings > Security > Git Fork Protection.
2. In GitHub, confirm the repository's visibility and fork policy.
3. From an owner-controlled second GitHub account, open a fork PR whose only change makes scripts/check_deploy.mjs print `Boolean(process.env.VERCEL_AUTOMATION_BYPASS_SECRET)` and `git rev-parse HEAD`, never the value. Authorize the Vercel preview if prompted.
4. In the resulting 'Deploy smoke' run, check whether it was triggered by deployment_status, whether the checked-out sha is the fork commit, and whether the boolean is true.
5. To learn whether workflow definitions come from the deployment commit, the same fork commit may add a workflow `on: deployment_status` that prints only `${{ secrets.SUPABASE_TEST_AUDIT_DATABASE_URL != '' }}`.
6. Close the PR afterwards, and rotate the bypass secret, plus any secret shown as present to fork code.
